title: Path Dependence
hook: Half the rules in your business exist because of a choice someone made years ago. Nobody remembers why.
statement: Where you are today is shaped by past decisions that still limit what you can do now.
explainer: Old tools, old pricing, old processes stick around because switching feels expensive. That's why new competitors with no baggage move faster. Some of those limits you can choose to undo.
sop: List the constraints on your business right now.
Mark which were past choices and which are real limits.
Estimate the cost to switch for each.
For new decisions, favor the ones you can reverse.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Past Choices 7, Switching Cost 8, Inertia 6. (7 + 8 + 6) ÷ 3 = 7.0. Higher means you're locked into old decisions, useful or not. Lower means you're free to redesign without much cost.
question: Name one rule in your business that only exists because of an old decision, then decide to keep or kill it.
closing_statement: Old decisions keep voting on today unless you unwind them.
caption:
Principle Nº 317: Path Dependence
